DOL PERM labor certification proposed rule (not yet finalized)—comment period closing; major implications for H-1B and employer-sponsored green cards
State Department immigrant visa processing freeze for 75 countries and public charge rule enforcement rollout—court challenges expected

items.title: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.feedTitle: Nvidia board unanimously reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman
items.summary: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO and chairman after he had resigned amid an alleged foreign intelligence operation targeting him. Trump, who has a close relationship with Huang, called for the reinstatement and took credit for the board's decision. The move has sparked congressional criticism and raised concerns about the administration's involvement in corporate governance.

items.title: Democratic Rep. Jimmy Gomez resigns after ethics probe
items.feedTitle: Democrat Gomez resigns from House after sexual misconduct report
items.summary: Rep. Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.) resigned from Congress after the House Ethics Committee found 'substantial evidence' he engaged in sexual misconduct, including making unwelcome sexual advances and sexual contact with a House staffer. The report documented harassment of a staff member, leading Gomez to step down immediately.

items.title: Trump defers Iowa toxic detonation to federal court
items.feedTitle: Trump says Army will not detonate bomb-making chemicals in Iowa without court approval
items.summary: President Trump said the Army will not proceed with detonating degraded bomb-making material (lead azide) at an Iowa ammunition plant without court approval, deferring the decision to a federal appeals court. The detonation had raised environmental concerns, with potential lead particle plumes extending up to 100 miles, prompting objections from residents and lawmakers.

items.title: Federal appeals court gives Trump path to dismiss hush money conviction
items.feedTitle: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump a path to erasing hush money conviction
items.summary: A federal appeals court decision moves Trump's hush money case to federal court, where he could seek dismissal of charges on immunity grounds. The ruling provides a potential legal pathway for Trump to overturn his conviction in the case.

items.title: DOJ admits deporting U.S. citizen to Mexico wrongly
items.feedTitle: DOJ says it deported US citizen to Mexico
items.summary: The Department of Justice admitted in federal court that the Trump administration deported a U.S. citizen, Brian José Morales García, to Mexico after officials incorrectly identified him as undocumented. The case raises questions about immigration enforcement procedures and vetting protocols under the new administration.

stlouis.title: Iowa munitions detonation raises St. Louis area concerns
stlouis.feedTitle: Iowa munitions plant detonation raises concerns in St. Louis area
stlouis.summary: The planned Army detonation of toxic explosives at an Iowa ammunition facility has raised concerns in the St. Louis area over potential lead exposure and environmental impact. Missouri Republicans had already objected to the plan before Trump intervened to pause it, citing safety risks and court rulings.

stlouis.title: Teen killed, two critically injured in Midtown shooting
stlouis.feedTitle: 14-year-old boy and 27-year-old woman dead, 16-year-old critically injured in Midtown St. Louis shooting
stlouis.summary: A 14-year-old was killed and two others critically injured in a shooting in Midtown St. Louis. The incident represents ongoing violence in the metro area.

stlouis.title: Illinois State Police arrest 12, recover 6 guns in Metro East
stlouis.feedTitle: Illinois State Police make 12 arrests, recover 6 guns in Metro East sweep
stlouis.summary: Illinois State Police made 12 arrests and recovered 6 firearms during a crime suppression detail in the Metro East area near St. Louis. The operation was part of ongoing efforts to combat gun violence in the region.

items.title: Ukraine strikes Russian warship in Libya with naval drones
items.feedTitle: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
items.summary: Ukraine confirmed it deployed seven naval drones in strikes on two Russian vessels off the coast of Libya, sinking the corvette Merkury and hitting a cargo ship. President Zelenskyy praised the 'exemplary' operation, which demonstrates Ukraine's expanding reach in targeting Russian military assets far from its territory.

items.title: COP31 climate talks collapse without fossil fuel agreement
items.feedTitle: What failure of COP31 reveals about a divided world
items.summary: The longest UN climate summit in history ended without reaching a keystone deal—the first failure in 17 years. Negotiations broke down over whether to include language about phasing out fossil fuels, the main driver of global warming, amid disputes over finance and opposition from oil-producing nations.

items.title: U.S. escalates sanctions targeting Iran shadow banking networks
items.feedTitle: US escalates sanctions on Iran, targets ‘shadow banking’ networks
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury announced sweeping sanctions on Iranian entities and over two dozen individuals, targeting what officials call 'shadow banking' networks worth nearly $15 billion. The move aims to disrupt Tehran's global financial activities and its ability to fund military operations.

items.title: Danish top court backs hardline 'ghetto law' evictions
items.feedTitle: Danish top court’s ‘ghetto law’ ruling supports hardline immigration policy
items.summary: Denmark's supreme court upheld the country's controversial 'ghetto law' allowing eviction of 'non-Western' families from certain neighborhoods, finding it did not constitute discrimination. The ruling supports one of Europe's hardest-line immigration policies.

items.title: Iran flogs singer for performing without hijab
items.feedTitle: Iran flogs singer Parastoo Ahmadi for performing without headscarf
items.summary: Iranian authorities carried out flogging sentences of 74 lashes each against singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four production team members for performing without headscarf, violating public decency laws. The singers also face two-year bans on travel and artistic activity, and Western governments have condemned the punishment as torture.

items.title: India pledges $1.6 billion flood relief to Nepal
items.feedTitle: India pledges $1.6bn in flood relief for Nepal as Balendra Shah visits Modi
items.summary: India pledged $1.6 billion in flood relief and announced major connectivity and development projects during Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah's first state visit to India since taking office in March. The visit included the flag-off of a new Ayodhya-Janakpur train service, marking a reset in India-Nepal ties.

items.title: FSSAI orders nationwide check on all bottled water brands
items.feedTitle: 'Unsafe' Bisleri bottled water sample prompts India to check all brands
items.summary: India's food safety regulator ordered inspections of all packaged drinking water brands after an 'unsafe' sample of Bisleri bottled water prompted nationwide checks. Bisleri has disputed the findings, saying its water is safe for consumption, as the FSSAI moves forward with prosecution proceedings.

items.title: Kerala police probe fairness cream linked to kidney failure
items.feedTitle: Kerala: Police investigate fairness cream's alleged link to kidney ailment in 17-year-old Indian girl
items.summary: Kerala police are investigating the alleged connection between a mercury-laced fairness cream and kidney ailment in a 17-year-old girl. The case highlights risks of unregulated cosmetic products and influencer promotion of unsafe skincare items, prompting regulatory action against sellers.

items.title: Chinese satellites made unusual manoeuvres over Pahalgam before terror attack
items.feedTitle: Exclusive-Chinese satellite doubled passes over Pahalgam 6 days before terror attack
items.summary: According to an exclusive report, a Chinese satellite doubled its passes over Pahalgam and made 37 unusual manoeuvres in the six days before a 2025 terror attack in the region. The findings suggest the manoeuvres were likely planned in advance and raise questions about surveillance preceding the incident.

items.title: Supreme Court grants Godhra train burning convict medical bail
items.feedTitle: SC grants bail to Godhra train burning convict on medical grounds
items.summary: India's Supreme Court granted bail on medical grounds to a life convict in the 2002 Godhra train burning case, suspending his sentence temporarily. The decision marks a rare grant of medical bail in a high-profile communal violence case.

immigration.title: Labor Department proposes sweeping PERM certification changes
immigration.feedTitle: Modernizing the Labor Market Test and Improving Protections for U.S. Workers in the PERM Immigrant Visa Program
immigration.summary: The U.S. Department of Labor has proposed major overhaul of the PERM labor certification process governing permanent employment-based green cards. The proposed rule (not yet final) would extend recruitment periods to 90 days, impose a 2-year layoff bar on employers, and end the Schedule A fast-track for nurses and healthcare workers—major changes to employer-sponsored immigration affecting H-1B and permanent visa holders.

immigration.title: Trump ICE revives decades-old cases to deport green card holders
immigration.feedTitle: Trump’s ICE is reviving decades-old cases to deport green card holders
immigration.summary: Immigration Customs Enforcement under Trump is reviving decades-old deportation cases against green card holders, using old records to initiate removal proceedings. The practice signals a broad enforcement shift targeting even long-term permanent residents.

immigration.title: State Department suspends immigrant visas for 75 high-risk countries
immigration.feedTitle: Update: State Dep't Pause on Immigrant Visas for Nationals of 75 Countries "At High Risk of Public Charge Usage"
immigration.summary: The State Department announced a pause on immigrant visa processing for nationals of 75 countries deemed 'at high risk of public charge usage,' suspending interviews worldwide pending officer retraining on updated public charge rules. The measure is a significant departure from previous visa adjudication standards and remains in effect pending further guidance.

items.title: Nvidia shares surge 31%, adding nearly $1 trillion in value
items.feedTitle: Stock Market Today, Nov. 23: Nvidia Surges 31%, Adding Nearly $1 Trillion in Market Value as Jensen Huang Reclaims CEO Role
items.summary: Nvidia's stock jumped 31% on November 23 following CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement, adding approximately $950 billion to $1 trillion in market value. The rally fueled a broad market rebound, with the S&P 500 gaining 4.7% and Nasdaq rising 6.5% in what was the best day for US stocks in more than a year, partially recovering from last week's losses.

items.title: Oil prices fall as Middle East crude supplies continue flowing
items.feedTitle: Oil Futures Extend Decline as Middle East Crude Continues to Flow
items.summary: Oil futures extended their decline as crude continued to flow from the Middle East despite regional tensions, with traders weighing ample supply against geopolitical risks. Prices remain under pressure as markets assess ongoing disruptions in the Gulf against increased production elsewhere.

items.title: Indian stocks plunge 1.8%; Sensex sheds 1,484 points in sell-off
items.feedTitle: Indian Stocks Plunge Nearly 2% as Sensex Sheds 1,484 Points, Investors Lose $5.7 Billion
items.summary: India's benchmark Sensex index fell 1,484 points (1.8%) in heavy selling, with the Nifty dropping below 25,400 amid profit-taking after a four-week rally. Banking and metal stocks led declines, wiping out ₹5.6 trillion in investor wealth—the worst single-day fall in four months.

items.title: Huang's return valued at $2.8 trillion for Nvidia
items.feedTitle: $2.8 trillion: The value of Huang's return to Nvidia
items.summary: Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has been valued at approximately $2.8 trillion in terms of market impact. The dramatic reversal of his resignation, followed by stock gains exceeding 30%, signals investor confidence in his leadership and the AI sector's growth trajectory.

items.title: Anthropic options post solid debut despite AI sector volatility
items.feedTitle: Anthropic options post solid debut, trailing SpaceX record
items.summary: Anthropic's options began trading with solid volume in its market debut, though the AI startup's stock fell during its second day of trading as investors rotated into Nvidia and other chip-related plays. The IPO underperformed the broader AI rally driven by Huang's return, raising questions about valuation expectations.

finance.note: US stocks rebounded sharply on November 23, with the Dow gaining 3% and Nasdaq jumping 6.5% following Jensen Huang's reinstatement at Nvidia, which surged 31%; oil prices fell as Middle East crude continued flowing despite regional tensions. India's Sensex tumbled 1.8% in heavy profit-taking after a four-week rally. Watch for Senate Banking Committee testimony from Huang on December 3, escalating federal scrutiny around Nvidia's governance and export controls; ongoing concerns about AI sector valuations post-rebound; and global trade frictions as COP31 climate talks collapsed.

cards.title: Constraints Enable Innovation
cards.insight: Tight deadlines, limited resources, or unexpected obstacles often spark creative breakthroughs. Rather than stifle imagination, constraints force teams to think laterally, discard assumptions, and discover novel solutions that abundant freedom might never have revealed.
cards.takeaway: Reframe project limitations not as barriers but as creative springboards—challenge teams to find elegant solutions within constraints rather than waiting for perfect conditions.

cards.title: Diversity Fuels Original Thinking
cards.insight: Creative insight emerges at the intersection of different perspectives, disciplines, and experiences. Homogeneous teams tend to reinforce existing patterns; diverse teams break them. The collision of unlike viewpoints generates cognitive friction that sparks novelty.
cards.takeaway: Deliberately compose teams with varied backgrounds, expertise, and thinking styles. Create forums where differing views are actively solicited and synthesized.

cards.title: Play Precedes Purpose
cards.insight: Creative work often begins with play—experimentation without immediate utility. Allowing space for exploration, failed experiments, and tangential curiosity creates the psychological safety and cognitive flexibility that genuine innovation requires.
cards.takeaway: Protect time for unstructured exploration; reward thoughtful failure; resist the urge to prematurely narrow focus toward predetermined outcomes.

cards.title: Creativity Requires Friction, Not Flow
cards.insight: While 'flow state' feels productive, genuine creativity often demands struggle, doubt, and productive discomfort. The tension between competing ideas, the friction of critique, and the dissonance of unsolved problems activate deeper creative thinking.
cards.takeaway: Embrace constructive tension in creative processes. Seek feedback early, encourage respectful disagreement, and resist premature convergence on comfortable solutions.

ai.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship for code review automation
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic launches Claude Ship, letting AI agents review, fix, and approve code changes
ai.summary: Anthropic unveiled Claude Ship, a tool enabling Claude AI agents to autonomously review, fix, and approve code pull requests, automating routine developer tasks. The product represents Anthropic's expansion into agentic AI and developer workflow automation.

ai.title: OpenAI and Cisco launch Shirudo for AI security infrastructure
ai.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source infrastructure shield designed to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks. The collaboration aims to safeguard critical systems from agentic AI threats by enabling cybersecurity systems to self-heal and defend against intelligent attacks.

ai.title: States sue SpaceX over Grok AI generating child sexual abuse material
ai.feedTitle: States sue Musk companies over flood of sexualized images made with AI chatbot Grok
ai.summary: Virginia and Oregon filed separate lawsuits against SpaceX, accusing the company of promoting Grok's 'spicy mode'—an unrestricted AI mode that generates sexualized and child sexual abuse material. The legal action signals growing scrutiny of AI safety guardrails and content moderation in large language models.

ai.title: Zhipu releases GLM-5.4 model with Loop Transformer architecture
ai.feedTitle: Z.ai unveils GLM-5.4 model with Loop Transformer design
ai.summary: Chinese AI lab Zhipu unveiled its GLM-5.4 flagship model featuring a novel Loop Transformer design and 750 billion parameters, expanding capabilities in multimodal AI with image input support. The release positions Zhipu as a contender in large model development alongside OpenAI and Anthropic.

ai.title: California AG Bonta sues OpenAI over AI model security
ai.feedTitle: California AG Bonta Sues OpenAI Over AI Model Security Concerns
ai.summary: California Attorney General Bonta filed a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging inadequate security measures and model vulnerabilities. The legal action reflects state-level regulatory pressure on AI companies to demonstrate robust safety and security practices.
